title: A machine-vision framework for electric vehicle charging hole localization based on contour-driven detection and geometric verification
content:
by Wei Luo, Qiantao Huo, Xin Li

The accurate localization of charging holes is an indispensable perception step for the automatic charging system of electric vehicles, since the success of subsequent charging-gun insertion depends directly on the precise estimation of the geometric centers of the holes on the vehicle charging interface. This paper presents a lightweight machine-vision framework for charging hole localization based on contour-driven detection and geometric verification. The proposed framework integrates image filtering, RGB-to-HSL color-space conversion, parameterized HSL adjustment, two-stage contour detection, minimum enclosing circle fitting, and Hough circle verification into a deterministic pipeline. The framework is interpretable, does not require a learning-based training process, and can be deployed on conventional CPU-based computing resources. The image data used in this study were acquired by a monocular RGB camera mounted on the charging robot end-effector, in the same sensing configuration in which the system is intended to operate. A total of 80 images were collected from six vehicles equipped with the same five-hole charging interface, under realistic variations of illumination, viewing angle, reflective interference, and background complexity. Detailed parameter selection rationale, a parameter perturbation analysis, and a condition-specific ablation analysis are reported. On an Intel Core i7-12700 CPU with 16 GB RAM and no GPU acceleration, the proposed framework achieves an overall mean localization error of 4.2 pixels and a 96.25% detection success rate, with an average per-image processing time of approximately 60 ms. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides accurate, robust, and engineering-deployable charging-hole localization for the target charging interface.
